newsitem.title: USA: Hartford cuts property taxes again - report.
newsitem.headline: Hartford cuts property taxes again - report.

text.p: Hartford is the only major Connecticut city to cut property taxes for three straight years, the Hartford Courant reported Wednesday.
The city council unanimously approved a 1-mill reduction at its meeting Tuesday, the Courant said.
The total 1997-98 spending plan is $406 million -- a two percent drop from this year's $414 million budget.
In the past four years, the capital city's spending has declined from $444 million to $406 million, a drop of eight percent.
The council has also added an extra $1 million for emergency demolition of abandoned buildings and $250,000 more for summer youth-recreation programs.
Mayor Mike Peters said it was significant that Hartford has figured out how to lower taxes while maintaining a smaller but reasonable safety net.
"This is unheard of in urban areas in Connecticut and throughout the country," Peters was quoted as saying. "This city is turning the corner."
The tax rate will now drop about three percent to 31.4 mills. The owner of a home assessed at $100,000 would save $100.
